newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COFFEE SLIPS, SEPT/NOV AGAIN AT DISCOUNT.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COFFEE SLIPS, SEPT/NOV AGAIN AT DISCOUNT.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were pinioned in maximum ranges of $20 on the two nearby contracts on Friday morning and the London market was again reluctant to track the strength in New York.
The gyrations of the Sept/Nov spread continued to attract attention as it fluctuated between premium and discount, and was nominally valued at $10 under by the midday break.
Other forward spreads stayed at a premium.
Commission house interest was noted on the buy side but trading was still extremely thin with just 1,080 lots on the board by the midday break.
September was down $14 at $1,630 after rising to a high of $1,650. November was down $6 at $1,640.
Traders had called the London market to open around $50 higher than Thursday's close but prices failed to make the due and opened $4 to $6 on nearby positions.
With the two markets moving independently of each other, eliminating interest in arbitrage activity, London traders said opens have been increasingly unpredictable.
Reduced buying interest due to a seasonal fall in demand could weaken nearby support for the spot September contract, they said.
"We're coming out of the summer period and the main robusta buyers are in the northern hemisphere," said one.
"There's no major rush to buy as (European) people are covered into September and October," he said.
